coverage_notes: WGI Government Effectiveness (2025 revision, 0-100) is the institutional proxy: quality of public services, civil service, policy formulation and implementation. It measures state capacity, not individual leaders — no subjective leader ratings. Capped PARTIAL: one governance dimension is not the whole leadership-capabilities concept (Sprint 6.21, DEC-041).

Live input: OECD tertiary attainment age 25-34 (ISCED 5-8, % of population, annual, Sprint 5.20). Attainment != enrollment. CHN has only 1 data point (2010); IND has 8 sparse data points. Still missing: secondary attainment/enrollment, learning outcomes/test scores, education quality, years of schooling, skills. One tertiary series cannot make Education AVAILABLE — capped at PARTIAL.

PARTIAL proxy (V1 Mission 1, delegated working model): the executable component measures RELATIVE ECONOMIC PARTICIPATION — labour force participation rate (ILO modeled, ages 15+) scored as a WDI-universe percentile. This is a narrow, labeled proxy for economic participation only; it is NOT a measurement of national character or determination. Resourcefulness, entrepreneurship and innovation dimensions remain unmeasured. PARTIAL ceiling enforced; higher participation is not universally positive (documented limitation).

World Bank WGI Rule of Law governance score (2025 revision, 0-100 absolute scale) live 1996-present for all 8 countries. Perception-based composite with measurement uncertainty; the 90% CI bounds and source counts are stored in the separate indicator_diagnostics evidence path and never become force inputs. This is a SOURCE indicator for the force, not an Atlas force score.

Source is WGI 'Control of Corruption' (2025 revision, 0-100): HIGHER means stronger control of corruption / less corruption — the raw stored value is never reversed or reinterpreted. Perception-based composite; uncertainty bounds/source counts are stored separately as indicator diagnostics. This is a SOURCE indicator, not an Atlas force score.

Investment & resource-allocation CONTEXT profile (Mission 4 §17): investment effort (GCF % of GDP), output growth, and labour productivity describe the input side — none of them measures allocation efficiency itself, and all three overlap productivity / infrastructure inputs by design (documented, not deduplicated).

Descriptive openness CONTEXT profile (Mission 4 §16): trade intensity (exports+imports % of GDP, exposed as derived TRADE_OPENNESS_GDP), external balance, current account, FDI inflows, plus population/GDP size context as candidates. Trade intensity is NOT strength (DEC-035) and these inputs overlap trade_capital_flows deliberately. The full force (capital, people, ideas) remains unmeasurable — no level score is claimed.

OECD labour productivity per hour (6/8 countries — CHN/IND are not OECD members and cannot receive an OECD-calibrated score). Sprint 6.14 (DEC-042 Option A — owner approved): level = mid-rank percentile within the versioned OECD universe oecd_lpph_v1, period-specific. Capped PARTIAL: OECD relative productivity position only — not the whole productivity/output-growth force, not a global percentile.

ULC growth is relative-cost meaningful; CPI inflation is a domestic price-pressure input. Relative international competitiveness ultimately needs exchange rates and partner-country price/cost comparisons — CPI alone (e.g. CHN/IND without OECD ULC) makes this force partial, never available.

World Bank WDI live (2000–2025, all 8 countries): exports/imports of goods and services, the published external balance (direct provider series for trade balance — not derived), and the current account. FDI net inflows (%GDP) live 1990+ all 8 countries (V1 Mission 1). Capital-flow measures beyond the current account and bilateral flows (UN Comtrade) come later.
World Bank gross capital formation live (2000–2025, all 8 countries) + fixed broadband per 100 (Mission 2). Investment effort + digital coverage context — NOT infrastructure quality.

Private-sector credit gap + debt service (BIS) + general-government gross debt (IMF WEO, Sprint 5.19). Government debt is a raw level input only — no monotonic 'higher debt = weaker' curve is approved; debt sustainability depends on interest cost, currency, maturity, fiscal capacity, monetary sovereignty, and growth (CONTEXTUAL_DEFERRED in the normalization registry). Sprint 6.13 (DEC-040, ratified) added a score: CONDITION_MINUS_PENALTY composition, level = clamp(DSR + (credit_gap - 50), 0, 100), force-aggregation-v0.4.

Live inputs are spending measures only (World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.CD / MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, underlying source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database). SIPRI describes military expenditure as an INPUT measure - resources absorbed by the military - not a measure of military capability or security. Personnel capability, equipment quality and quantity, technology, logistics, readiness, combat experience, alliances/force projection, and nuclear capability are not measured, so spending alone can never make this force AVAILABLE (DEC-009 ceiling).

Live inputs: World Bank Gini index (income inequality, irregular) + WID top 10% net personal wealth share (wealth concentration, annual, Sprint 5.20). Both are distributional measures — opportunity gaps and values/social polarization remain missing. The force is capped at PARTIAL until its conceptual scope is better covered. WID data_quality column preserved but NOT used for filtering (official semantics unverified).

Initial institutional/conflict-risk proxy: WGI 'Political Stability and Absence of Violence/Terrorism' governance score (2025 revision, 0-100) live 1996-2024 for all 8 countries. It does NOT measure every form of domestic conflict (polarization, protests, distributional tension) — the force is capped at PARTIAL while this proxy is the only input; later ACLED / event data may strengthen it. Perception-based composite; uncertainty bounds/source counts are stored separately as indicator diagnostics. SOURCE indicator, not an Atlas force score.

Structural context profile `geo_profile_v1` (landlocked status, coastline, island status, land area and maritime access) is available for all tracked countries. It is deliberately static context and has no live time-series input or score.

Verified structural exposure context (Mission 4 §18): WB EN.CLC.MDAT.ZS, an EM-DAT-derived % of population affected by droughts/floods/extreme temperatures averaged over 1990-2009 (published at 2009 only — no annual series). Pandemic and climate-change exposure have no legally accessible provider series ingested yet; missing values mean 'not published', never 'zero events'.

Investment & resource-allocation CONTEXT profile (Mission 4 §17): investment effort (GCF % of GDP), output growth, and labour productivity describe the input side — none of them measures allocation efficiency itself, and all three overlap productivity / infrastructure inputs by design (documented, not deduplicated).

Descriptive openness CONTEXT profile (Mission 4 §16): trade intensity (exports+imports % of GDP, exposed as derived TRADE_OPENNESS_GDP), external balance, current account, FDI inflows, plus population/GDP size context as candidates. Trade intensity is NOT strength (DEC-035) and these inputs overlap trade_capital_flows deliberately. The full force (capital, people, ideas) remains unmeasurable — no level score is claimed.

OECD labour productivity per hour (6/8 countries — CHN/IND are not OECD members and cannot receive an OECD-calibrated score). Sprint 6.14 (DEC-042 Option A — owner approved): level = mid-rank percentile within the versioned OECD universe oecd_lpph_v1, period-specific. Capped PARTIAL: OECD relative productivity position only — not the whole productivity/output-growth force, not a global percentile.

ULC growth is relative-cost meaningful; CPI inflation is a domestic price-pressure input. Relative international competitiveness ultimately needs exchange rates and partner-country price/cost comparisons — CPI alone (e.g. CHN/IND without OECD ULC) makes this force partial, never available.

World Bank WDI live (2000–2025, all 8 countries): exports/imports of goods and services, the published external balance (direct provider series for trade balance — not derived), and the current account. FDI net inflows (%GDP) live 1990+ all 8 countries (V1 Mission 1). Capital-flow measures beyond the current account and bilateral flows (UN Comtrade) come later.
World Bank gross capital formation live (2000–2025, all 8 countries) + fixed broadband per 100 (Mission 2). Investment effort + digital coverage context — NOT infrastructure quality.

Private-sector credit gap + debt service (BIS) + general-government gross debt (IMF WEO, Sprint 5.19). Government debt is a raw level input only — no monotonic 'higher debt = weaker' curve is approved; debt sustainability depends on interest cost, currency, maturity, fiscal capacity, monetary sovereignty, and growth (CONTEXTUAL_DEFERRED in the normalization registry). Sprint 6.13 (DEC-040, ratified) added a score: CONDITION_MINUS_PENALTY composition, level = clamp(DSR + (credit_gap - 50), 0, 100), force-aggregation-v0.4.

Live inputs are spending measures only (World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.CD / MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, underlying source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database). SIPRI describes military expenditure as an INPUT measure - resources absorbed by the military - not a measure of military capability or security. Personnel capability, equipment quality and quantity, technology, logistics, readiness, combat experience, alliances/force projection, and nuclear capability are not measured, so spending alone can never make this force AVAILABLE (DEC-009 ceiling).

Live inputs: World Bank Gini index (income inequality, irregular) + WID top 10% net personal wealth share (wealth concentration, annual, Sprint 5.20). Both are distributional measures — opportunity gaps and values/social polarization remain missing. The force is capped at PARTIAL until its conceptual scope is better covered. WID data_quality column preserved but NOT used for filtering (official semantics unverified).

Initial institutional/conflict-risk proxy: WGI 'Political Stability and Absence of Violence/Terrorism' governance score (2025 revision, 0-100) live 1996-2024 for all 8 countries. It does NOT measure every form of domestic conflict (polarization, protests, distributional tension) — the force is capped at PARTIAL while this proxy is the only input; later ACLED / event data may strengthen it. Perception-based composite; uncertainty bounds/source counts are stored separately as indicator diagnostics. SOURCE indicator, not an Atlas force score.

Structural context profile `geo_profile_v1` (landlocked status, coastline, island status, land area and maritime access) is available for all tracked countries. It is deliberately static context and has no live time-series input or score.

Verified structural exposure context (Mission 4 §18): WB EN.CLC.MDAT.ZS, an EM-DAT-derived % of population affected by droughts/floods/extreme temperatures averaged over 1990-2009 (published at 2009 only — no annual series). Pandemic and climate-change exposure have no legally accessible provider series ingested yet; missing values mean 'not published', never 'zero events'.

Live input: OECD tertiary attainment age 25-34 (ISCED 5-8, % of population, annual, Sprint 5.20). Attainment != enrollment. CHN has only 1 data point (2010); IND has 8 sparse data points. Still missing: secondary attainment/enrollment, learning outcomes/test scores, education quality, years of schooling, skills. One tertiary series cannot make Education AVAILABLE — capped at PARTIAL.

Resourcefulness, entrepreneurship and innovation dimensions remain unmeasured. PARTIAL ceiling enforced; higher participation is not universally positive (documented limitation).
